papers.title_en: BRACHIO: Broad Representations Across Centres for Head-and-neck Imaging Oncology (HECKTOR 2026)
papers.authors: Roxanne De Maeyer, Ine Dirks, Yannick Brackenier, Simon DeKeyser, Jef Vandemeulebroucke, Vicky De Ridder
papers.tldr: HECKTOR 2026 挑战赛要求在多中心 PET/CT 上进行头颈癌原发与淋巴结肿瘤勾画、TN 分期和 RFS 预测。nucli 团队利用自监督预训练的 PET-DINOv2-MIPs 编码器，分割端采用 DynUNet 与 SimMIM 预训练 SwinUNETR 集成。测试集平均 Dice 为 0.5409，T/N 分期平衡准确率 0.3962/0.6432，RFS 的 C-index 达 0.6577。预后结果接近上届最佳，但分割偏弱制约了分期表现。
papers.abstract_en: The HECKTOR 2026 challenge benchmarks machine learning for head and neck cancer, where teams delineate primary and nodal tumour volumes, perform TN staging, and predict recurrence-free survival (RFS). This report describes the submissions for the HECKTOR challenge of team nucli. As the three tasks span both dense and global information from multicentric PET/CT scans, we utilise self-supervised pre-trained encoders, training a 2D DINOv2 encoder (PET-DINOv2-MIPs) on HECKTOR 2026's PET scans. Our final test submission ensembles a DynUNet trained from scratch with a SwinUNETR whose Swin trunk was initialised from a SimMIM-pre-trained checkpoint for segmentation, reaching a mean Dice of 0.5409. For TN staging, GTVp/GTVn geometric features from the segmentation masks are fit to stage probabilities by logistic regression (LR) and fused with PET-DINOv2-MIPs deep features (PCA + LR) via a second-level LR, reaching balanced accuracies of 0.3962 (T-stage) and 0.6432 (N-stage). For the RFS prognosis task, we fine-tune the last two blocks of the PET-DINOv2-MIPs ViT-S encoder jointly with an MLP head under a CoxPH loss, concatenating clinical covariates with the imaging features, reaching a test Harrell's C-index of 0.6577 and a weighted challenge score of 0.5802. The prognosis result is comparable to the best entry of the previous edition and consistent with our internal cross-validation, while our segmentation result is well below it and limits the staging results that depend on it.

papers.title_en: RepConTUR: A Report-Conditioned Volumetric Multimodal Model for Abdominal Tumor Segmentation
papers.authors: Seunghwan Lee, Sangjoon Park, Jongmin Lee, Yoon Jo Kim, Wonyoung Cho, Jin Sung Kim, Han Joo Chae
papers.evidence: 面向放疗计划的报告条件三维肿瘤勾画
papers.tldr: 腹部肿瘤放疗勾画易受假阳性误差影响，现有文本提示模型多依赖短指代短语且以2D为主。RepConTUR以叙述性影像报告为条件，构建原生3D早期融合多模态模型，并联合训练RES、GSEG、报告生成和VQA。在肝、肾、胰腺上，其DSC、实例精度和检测F1优于文本提示基线，并在四个分布外队列平均指标领先。消融表明报告条件、联合GSEG训练和原生3D模块分别提升检测F1、RES F1和GSEG F1。
papers.abstract_en: Tumor delineation is required for radiotherapy planning, yet automatic segmentation is limited by errors, predominantly false positives, that distort dose and increase editing time. The radiology report accompanies the scan and localizes disease at the suborgan level, but existing text-promptable models condition on short referring phrases, and most operate in 2D. We present RepConTUR, a single native-3D early-fusion multimodal model that conditions volumetric abdominal tumor segmentation on the narrative report. We extend AbdomenAtlas 3.0 to a suborgan-level promptable segmentation dataset and generate report-based VQA pairs, yielding four report-derived tasks on the same annotations: referring segmentation (RES), report-grounded segmentation (GSEG), report generation (RRG), and visual question answering (VQA). We train RepConTUR, comprising a 3D CT encoder, an early-fusion language model, and a native-3D segmentation module, jointly on the four tasks. Across liver, kidney and pancreas, RepConTUR attains the highest Dice similarity coefficient (DSC), instance-wise precision, and detection F1 among the text-promptable baselines, and adding the report raises mean precision while leaving recall comparable. Against two vision-only specialists, nnU-Net and the report-supervised R-Super, RepConTUR attains the highest value on every in-domain metric for liver and pancreas and the highest mean DSC, recall, precision, and detection F1 over the four out-of-distribution public cohorts. Ablations indicate that conditioning on the narrative report raises detection F1 from 0.499 to 0.528 within the same model, that joint GSEG training raises RES F1 from 0.450 to 0.482, and that the native-3D segmentation module raises GSEG F1 from 0.139 to 0.528 over its 2D counterpart. Code is available at https://github.com/Oncosoft-Research/RepConTUR.

papers.title_en: Anatomical Prior-Guided Routing for 3D Lung Tumor Segmentation
papers.authors: Uihyeon Maeng, Jonghun Kim, Hyunjin Park
papers.evidence: 用于治疗计划的CT三维肺肿瘤分割
papers.tldr: 3D肺肿瘤分割受肿瘤占比小、解剖位置异质性影响，且patch训练与滑窗推理削弱全局解剖上下文。为此提出解剖先验引导路由模块APRM：按图像块区域占用先验确定路由门，在共享专家适配器池上稀疏路由特征。两个数据集、多种骨干上均稳定优于基线，可视化显示特征响应随位置变化。该工作以轻量路由实现解剖特异适应并共享专家容量。
papers.abstract_en: Accurate lung tumor segmentation in computed tomography (CT) is essential for treatment planning, response assessment, and quantitative imaging analysis. However, 3D lung tumor segmentation remains challenging because tumors occupy only a small portion of the whole volume and exhibit heterogeneous appearances across anatomical locations. In patch-based training and sliding-window inference for 3D medical image segmentation, location-dependent heterogeneity is further amplified because cropped image patches provide limited global anatomical context, making it difficult for a model to adapt its feature processing according to the anatomical region from which each patch is extracted. To address this limitation, we propose an Anatomical Prior-guided Routing Module (APRM) for lung tumor segmentation. For each image patch, we obtain anatomical prior information of regional occupancy and deterministically select an anatomical routing gate. The selected gate then performs sparse feature routing over a shared expert adapter pool, enabling anatomy-specific feature adaptation while sharing expert capacity across regions. We evaluate APRM on two datasets with various backbone networks and demonstrate consistent improvements over baseline models. Furthermore, feature visualizations show that APRM produces different feature responses depending on patch location, indicating that the proposed routing mechanism effectively adapts feature processing according to anatomical context.

papers.title_en: Morphology-Aware Channel-Decoupled Mamba Network for Medical Image Segmentation
papers.evidence: 面向治疗计划的CT多器官分割，形态感知Mamba网络
papers.tldr: CT多器官分割受器官形态差异大、组织对比低和边界模糊制约。本文提出MCDNet，以形态感知通道解耦状态空间模块分组建模，并用变形卷积与通道注意力增强局部结构。在Synapse腹部CT上取得81.61%平均Dice，验证了局部形态增强与长程依赖结合的有效性。该工作为异质解剖结构分割提供了可借鉴的高效建模思路。
papers.abstract_en: Accurate multi-organ segmentation in computed tomography (CT) is essential for computer-aided diagnosis, treatment planning, and disease monitoring. However, substantial variations in organ shape and size, together with low tissue contrast and ambiguous boundaries, complicate the modeling of heterogeneous anatomical structures. To address these challenges, we propose a Morphology-Aware Channel-Decoupled Mamba Network (MCDNet), which integrates adaptive local structural enhancement with channel-decoupled long-range modeling. Specifically, we introduce a Morphology-Aware Channel-Decoupled State-Space (MCSS) block that divides feature channels into separate processing groups, allowing differentiated structural representations to be learned within an efficient state-space framework. Within each group, a Morphology-Aware Enhancement Module (MAEM) combines deformable convolutions with channel attention to adapt local feature extraction to anatomical shape variations. Group-wise state-space modeling then captures long-range spatial dependencies, and channel gating adaptively integrates the resulting features. Experiments on the Synapse abdominal CT dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of MCDNet, achieving an average Dice Similarity Coefficient of 81.61% for multi-organ segmentation.

papers.title_en: A 211K Parameter Foundation Model: Genetic Prompting in Neural Cellular Automata
papers.authors: John Kalkhof, Niklas Ihm, Daniel Kirste, Anirban Mukhopadhyay
papers.evidence: 无需重训练即可适配多种医学分割任务的轻量基础模型
papers.tldr: 现代基础模型依赖大规模参数，SAM 等医学分割模型难以在低资源环境部署。作者提出 Foundational-NCA，基于神经细胞自动机，用遗传提示机制在潜任务空间中做梯度学习与遗传优化，以紧凑任务向量引导预测。模型仅 21.1 万参数，在 TotalSegmentator 的 15 个已训任务上平均 Dice 达 84.5%，6 个未见任务为 60.4%。相比 SAM 类模型缩小逾 180 倍，展示了超紧凑模型实现任务泛化的可行性。
papers.abstract_en: The scale of modern foundation models enables broad task generalization. In medical imaging, where segmentation demands vary widely across clinical contexts, such flexibility is invaluable. But current models, such as SAM trade adaptability for scale, locking their utility behind high-end infrastructure and leaving behind the low-resource environments most in need of diagnostic support. To bridge this gap, we introduce Foundational-NCA, a lightweight foundation model capable of adapting to a wide range of medical segmentation tasks without retraining. Built on Neural Cellular Automata (NCA), Foundational-NCA incorporates gradient-based learning with genetic optimization over a latent task space, using a compact task vector to guide predictions. This enables dynamic adaptation via a genetic prompt mechanism, allowing the model to generalize across tasks while keeping the parameter count magnitudes lower at just 211 thousand, compared to SAM-based models with 38.9 to 636 million parameters. We evaluate Foundational-NCA on 15 trained and 6 entirely unseen segmentation tasks from the TotalSegmentator dataset, achieving an average Dice score of 84.5% on known tasks and 60.4% on unseen ones. These results demonstrate that task generalization is possible in ultra-compact models, laying the groundwork for resource-efficient, deployable foundation models in clinical environments where infrastructure is limited. By reducing model size by over 180 times, Foundational-NCA takes a step toward a more equitable future for medical AI, one where powerful tools are within reach of every healthcare setting.

papers.title_en: Segment Anything Model Based Context Guided Mamba Unet for Medical Image Segmentation
papers.evidence: 融合SAM与Mamba的通用医学图像分割框架，可迁移至放疗靶区与危及器官分割
papers.tldr: 医学图像分割需兼顾全局上下文与细粒度结构，SAM泛化强但医学域适应不足，Mamba长程建模高效却易丢失解剖细节。为此提出SAMBA-UNet，将SAM上下文知识与Mamba层级特征学习融合，并用HCEM注意力模块深度整合多级特征。结合LoRA与Adapter微调增强域适应与鲁棒性。在Synapse、ISIC17、ISIC18上取得SOTA，兼顾泛化性、分割精度与计算效率。
papers.abstract_en: Medical image segmentation is crucial for clinical diagnosis and treatment planning, requiring both global contextual understanding and fine-grained structural precision. While the Segment Anything Model (SAM) demonstrates strong generalization capabilities, its direct application to medical images often lacks domain-specific adaptability. Meanwhile, State Space Models (SSMs)-based methods, such as Mamba, efficiently capture long-range dependencies but may struggle with preserving fine anatomical details. To address these challenges, we propose a segment anything model based context guided mamba unet, SAMBA-UNet, a novel framework that integrates SAM's context knowledge with Mamba's hierarchical feature learning to enhance both global representation and local detail refinement. Specifically, we introduce the Hierarchical Context Enhancement Module (HCEM), an attention-based fusion module that deeply incorporates the multi-level features of SAM and Mamba to improve detail perception and segmentation precision. Additionally, we employ LoRA and Adapter-based fine-tuning to adapt SAM to medical imaging tasks, further enhancing its domain-specific segmentation capability and robustness. We conducted a comprehensive study on several medical segmentation datasets, including Synapse, ISIC17, and ISIC18, evaluating our method across multiple metrics. Experimental results demonstrate that SAMBA-UNet achieves state-of-the-art performance, effectively balancing generalization, segmentation accuracy, and computational efficiency. Our code will be released upon acceptance.
